title: "Live Demo: K-Means Clustering"

## Explore the worker segments

This is an interactive view of the K-Means model from the Predictive Modeling page, kept on its own so you can play with it without scrolling through the full analysis. Each point is a worker placed by age and annual wage, the two features the model used, and colored by the segment K-Means assigned. The black diamonds are the cluster centroids, the center points the algorithm computed for each segment.

Two ways to interact. Use the dropdown to isolate a single segment, or choose "All segments" to see them together. You can also click any entry in the legend to hide or show that segment, and you can box-zoom into any region of the chart. The points shown here are a representative sample so the page stays responsive; the full version that plots all 1.49 million workers runs in the notebook `analysis/ml_kmeans_julie.ipynb`.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-cap: "Interactive K-Means demo. Use the dropdown to isolate a segment, click legend entries to toggle them, and box-zoom to inspect. Black diamonds are centroids."
import sys, pathlib
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio
pio.templates.default = "plotly_white"

root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
while not (root / "_quarto.yml").exists() and root != root.parent:
    root = root.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(root / "analysis"))
from utils import apply_theme, PROCESSED

profile = pd.read_csv(PROCESSED / "kmeans_cluster_profile.csv")
profile = profile.sort_values("wgt_avg_wage").reset_index(drop=True)
SEGMENTS = ["Low-wage, early career", "Mid-wage, late career",
            "High-wage professional", "Elite earners"]
profile["segment"] = SEGMENTS[: len(profile)]
cluster_to_segment = dict(zip(profile["cluster"], profile["segment"]))

samp = pd.read_csv(PROCESSED / "kmeans_scatter_sample.csv")
samp["segment"] = samp["cluster"].map(cluster_to_segment)
COLORS = dict(zip(SEGMENTS, ["#2c7bb6", "#fdae61", "#1a9641", "#d7191c"]))

fig = go.Figure()
for seg in SEGMENTS:
    s = samp[samp["segment"] == seg]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(
        x=s["AGE"], y=s["INCWAGE"], mode="markers", name=seg,
        marker=dict(size=5, opacity=0.5, color=COLORS[seg]),
    ))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=profile["wgt_avg_age"], y=profile["wgt_avg_wage"], mode="markers",
    name="Centroid", hovertext=profile["segment"], hoverinfo="text",
    marker=dict(symbol="diamond", size=15, color="black"),
))

n = len(SEGMENTS)
def visibility(active):
    seg_vis = [True] * n if active is None else [i == active for i in range(n)]
    return seg_vis + [True]            # centroid trace always on

buttons = [dict(label="All segments", method="update",
                args=[{"visible": visibility(None)}])]
for i, seg in enumerate(SEGMENTS):
    buttons.append(dict(label=seg, method="update",
                        args=[{"visible": visibility(i)}]))

fig.update_layout(
    updatemenus=[dict(buttons=buttons, x=0.0, xanchor="left",
                      y=1.15, yanchor="top", showactive=True)],
    xaxis_title="Age", yaxis_title="Annual wage (USD)",
    title="K-Means worker segments (interactive)",
)
apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```

## What to look for

Switching between segments makes the model's logic concrete. The low-wage and mid-wage segments sit as broad bands near the bottom and are close to gender balanced, the high-wage professional band sits clearly above them, and the elite segment is a thin scatter far up the wage axis. Isolating the elite segment shows how few workers reach it and, on the full analysis page, how strongly male it skews. The centroids mark where each segment centers, which is exactly the average age and wage of its members.

## Overcharged map: filter by segment, career stage, and gender

This map is fully filterable. Pick a wage **segment**, a **career stage**, and which **gender** share to color by, and the choropleth recolors instantly for any combination of the three. The three controls are independent, so you can ask, for example, what the female share of the elite segment looks like among only late-career workers. The color scale is locked to a fixed zero to one hundred percent range, so a given shade always means the same percentage no matter which filters are active, rather than rescaling and shifting under you.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
# Prepare the fine-grained data (state x segment x career stage x sex) for the
# client-side Observable dashboard and the animation below.
ABBR_FIPS = {
    "AL": "01", "AK": "02", "AZ": "04", "AR": "05", "CA": "06", "CO": "08",
    "CT": "09", "DE": "10", "DC": "11", "FL": "12", "GA": "13", "HI": "15",
    "ID": "16", "IL": "17", "IN": "18", "IA": "19", "KS": "20", "KY": "21",
    "LA": "22", "ME": "23", "MD": "24", "MA": "25", "MI": "26", "MN": "27",
    "MS": "28", "MO": "29", "MT": "30", "NE": "31", "NV": "32", "NH": "33",
    "NJ": "34", "NM": "35", "NY": "36", "NC": "37", "ND": "38", "OH": "39",
    "OK": "40", "OR": "41", "PA": "42", "RI": "44", "SC": "45", "SD": "46",
    "TN": "47", "TX": "48", "UT": "49", "VT": "50", "VA": "51", "WA": "53",
    "WV": "54", "WI": "55", "WY": "56",
}
import json
stage_df = pd.read_csv(PROCESSED / "state_segment_stage_sex.csv")
stage_df["segment"] = stage_df["cluster"].map(cluster_to_segment)
stage_df["fips"] = stage_df["STATE_CODE"].map(ABBR_FIPS)

# Round-trip through JSON so OJS receives native types (pandas/numpy
# scalars are not directly JSON-serializable by ojs_define).
dash_records = json.loads(
    stage_df[["fips", "STATE_CODE", "segment", "career_stage", "sex", "weighted"]]
    .to_json(orient="records")
)
ojs_define(dashdata=dash_records)
ojs_define(segment_opts=["All segments"] + list(SEGMENTS))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
us = fetch("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/us-atlas@3/states-10m.json").then(r => r.json())
topojson = require("topojson-client@3")
statesFC = topojson.feature(us, us.objects.states)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof segSel = Inputs.select(segment_opts, {label: "Segment", value: "All segments"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof stageSel = Inputs.select(["All stages", "Early (<35)", "Mid (35-54)", "Late (55+)"], {label: "Career stage", value: "All stages"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sexSel = Inputs.select(["Female", "Male"], {label: "Show share of", value: "Female"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
shares = {
  const rows = dashdata.filter(d =>
    (segSel === "All segments" || d.segment === segSel) &&
    (stageSel === "All stages" || d.career_stage === stageSel));
  return d3.rollup(rows,
    v => {
      const tot = d3.sum(v, d => d.weighted);
      const f = d3.sum(v.filter(d => d.sex === "Female"), d => d.weighted);
      return tot ? 100 * (sexSel === "Female" ? f : (tot - f)) / tot : null;
    },
    d => d.fips);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  projection: "albers-usa",
  width: 820,
  color: {scheme: "blues", domain: [0, 100], legend: true, label: `% ${sexSel}`},
  marks: [
    Plot.geo(statesFC.features, {
      fill: d => shares.get(d.id) ?? "#eeeeee",
      stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.5,
      title: d => `${d.properties.name}: ${shares.get(d.id) == null ? "n/a" : shares.get(d.id).toFixed(1) + "%"}`
    })
  ]
})
```

## Animated map: watch it shift across career stages

This view uses Plotly's animation button. Press **Play** to cycle the map through the three career stages and watch the female share of the workforce change with age, or drag the slider to a stage yourself. As above, the color scale is fixed from zero to one hundred percent so the frames are directly comparable.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-cap: "Animated choropleth. Press Play to cycle Early, Mid, and Late career stages. Color is the female share of all workers in each state, fixed on a 0 to 100 percent scale."
import plotly.express as px
g = (stage_df.groupby(["STATE_CODE", "career_stage", "sex"])["weighted"]
     .sum().reset_index())
piv = (g.pivot_table(index=["STATE_CODE", "career_stage"], columns="sex",
                     values="weighted", fill_value=0).reset_index())
piv["pct_female"] = (100 * piv["Female"] / (piv["Female"] + piv["Male"])).round(1)
stage_order = ["Early (<35)", "Mid (35-54)", "Late (55+)"]

anim = px.choropleth(
    piv, locations="STATE_CODE", locationmode="USA-states",
    color="pct_female", animation_frame="career_stage",
    category_orders={"career_stage": stage_order},
    scope="usa", color_continuous_scale="Blues", range_color=[0, 100],
    labels={"pct_female": "% female"},
    title="Female share of workers by career stage",
)
apply_theme(anim)
anim.show()
```
